title: Google Cloud Generative AI Leader
description: Google Cloud Generative AI Leader: a business-level, no-code fluency in generative AI -- core concepts, Google Cloud's gen AI product landscape, techniques that improve model output, and the business strategy and security/responsible-AI considerations behind a successful gen AI initiative.

units.title: Fundamentals of Gen AI
units.gate: Given a gen AI term or a data question, define it precisely -- not with another buzzword -- and say which stage of the ML lifecycle it belongs to.

objectives.text: Defining core gen AI concepts: artificial intelligence, natural language processing, machine learning, generative AI, foundation models, multimodal foundation models, diffusion models, prompt tuning, prompt engineering, large language models
Describing ML approaches: supervised, unsupervised, reinforcement
Identifying the stages of the ML lifecycle -- data ingestion, data preparation, model training, model deployment, model management -- and the Google Cloud tool for each
Choosing the appropriate foundation model for a business use case: modality, context window, security, availability/reliability, cost, performance, fine-tuning, customization
Identifying business use cases where gen AI creates, summarizes, discovers, or automates: text, image, code, and video generation, data analysis, personalized experience
Explaining the characteristics and importance of data quality and accessibility: completeness, consistency, relevance, availability, cost, format
Differentiating structured from unstructured data, with real-world examples of each
Differentiating labeled from unlabeled data
Identifying the core layers of the gen AI landscape: infrastructure, models, platforms, agents, applications
Identifying the use cases and strengths of Google's own foundation models: Gemini, Gemma, Imagen, Veo

units.title: Google Cloud's Gen AI Offerings
units.gate: Given a business need, name the specific Google Cloud gen AI product that fits it -- not just 'Google has an AI for that.'

objectives.text: Describing how Google's AI-first approach translates into its gen AI solutions
Describing what makes Google Cloud's AI platform enterprise-ready: responsible, secure, private, reliable, scalable
Recognizing the advantages of Google's integrated AI ecosystem across products and services
Describing the benefits of Google Cloud's open approach to AI
Identifying the components of Google Cloud's AI-optimized infrastructure: AI Hypercomputer, custom TPUs, GPUs, data centers
Explaining how Google Cloud's AI platform gives users control over their data: security, privacy, governance, open first-party models, pre-built and customizable solutions, agents
Describing how Google Cloud democratizes AI development: low-code and no-code tools, pre-trained models, APIs
Recognizing the functionality, use cases, and business value of the Gemini app and Gemini Advanced, including Gems
Recognizing the functionality, use cases, and business value of Gemini Enterprise: Notebook API, multimodal search, custom agent capabilities
Recognizing the functionality, use cases, and business value of Gemini for Google Workspace
Recognizing the functionality, use cases, and business value of Google Cloud's external search offerings: Agent Search on the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, Google Search

Recognizing the functionality, use cases, and business value of Google's Customer Engagement Suite: Conversational Agents, Agent Assist, Conversational Insights, Google Cloud Contact Center as a Service
Recognizing the functionality, use cases, and business value of the Agent Platform: Model Garden, Agent Search, Agent Platform AutoML
Recognizing the functionality, use cases, and business value of Google Cloud's RAG offerings: prebuilt RAG with Agent Search, RAG APIs
Recognizing the functionality, use cases, and business value of building custom agents on the Agent Platform
Identifying how agents use tools to interact with the external environment: extensions, functions, data stores, plugins
Identifying Google Cloud services and pre-built AI APIs used for agent tooling
Choosing between Agent Studio and Google AI Studio

units.title: Techniques to Improve Gen AI Model Output
units.gate: Given a foundation model limitation, name the specific technique -- grounding, RAG, prompting, fine-tuning -- that actually addresses it.

objectives.text: Identifying common foundation model limitations: data dependency, knowledge cutoff, bias, fairness, hallucinations, edge cases
Describing Google Cloud-recommended practices to address model limitations: grounding, retrieval-augmented generation, prompt engineering, fine-tuning, human in the loop
Recognizing Google-recommended practices for continuously monitoring and evaluating gen AI models: automatic upgrades, KPIs, security patches, versioning, performance tracking, drift monitoring
Defining prompt engineering and its significance when working with LLMs
Identifying prompting techniques and their use cases: zero-shot, one-shot, few-shot, role prompting, prompt chaining
Identifying advanced prompting techniques and when to use them: chain-of-thought prompting, ReAct prompting
Describing grounding in LLMs, and differentiating grounding with first-party enterprise data, third-party data, and world data
Describing how retrieval-augmented generation affects a gen AI model's output
Identifying Google Cloud's grounding offerings: prebuilt RAG with Agent Search, RAG APIs, Grounding with Google Search
Identifying how sampling parameters control gen AI model behavior: token count, temperature, top-p, safety settings, output length

units.title: Business Strategies for a Successful Gen AI Solution
units.gate: Given an organization considering gen AI, say what actually has to happen -- choosing the right solution, securing it, measuring its impact -- not just 'adopt AI.'

objectives.text: Recognizing types of gen AI solutions: text generation, image generation, code generation, personalized user needs
Identifying the key factors that influence gen AI needs: business requirements, technical constraints
Choosing the right gen AI solution for a specific business need
Identifying the steps to integrate gen AI into an organization
Identifying techniques to measure the impact of a gen AI initiative
Explaining security considerations throughout the ML lifecycle
Identifying the purpose and benefits of Google's Secure AI Framework (SAIF)
Recognizing Google Cloud security tools and their purpose: secure-by-design infrastructure, IAM, Security Command Center, workload monitoring
Explaining the importance of responsible AI and transparency
Describing privacy considerations: privacy risks, data anonymization, pseudonymization
Describing the business implications of data quality, bias, and fairness
Describing the importance of accountability and explainability in AI systems
